title: Published ODE models of gene and protein pathways show several kinds of memory

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Published ODE models of gene and protein pathways show several kinds of memory

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In simulations of 35 published ODE models of gene regulatory networks and protein/metabolic pathways from BioModels, the networks show several distinct kinds of memory (UCS-based, pairing, transfer, associative and consolidation memory) in response to patterns of node stimulation.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Here, we characterize biological gene regulatory circuit models and protein pathways and find them capable of several different kinds of memory.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “Abstract”. Scope: 35 ODE pathway models from BioModels (bacteria, slime mould, yeast, plants, vertebrates, mammals)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-01: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.89

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The paper supplies explicit stimulation-response criteria and identifies a public model repository. Re-running the finite model suite is feasible, although exact reproduction may require reconstruction from methods and supplements.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Download the 35 specified ODE models, apply the published stimulation protocols, and count models and node triples meeting each explicit memory criterion. Failure to reproduce the reported memory classes would refute the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The functional definition of memory is broader than conventional biological memory.

Reimplementation details and solver choices may affect threshold-crossing cases.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.9
analysis feasibility: 0.78
discriminating power: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.95
data adequacy: 0.88

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The five memory assays and the regulation thresholds are specified in the methods, the pathway models are in BioModels, and the authors' MATLAB suite is public, so re-running the survey is analysis rather than new research. The job is large and cluster-oriented, and the code is described as temporary, but a small team could rerun the suite. Agreement on which memory types occur would settle the claim as stated about these models.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Re-simulate the 35 BioModels ODE pathways with the published UCS/CS/response assays and count, for each model, which of the five memory labels appear under the paper's up- and down-regulation criteria. Finding several of those labels across the set would confirm the claim; finding only one label, or none, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The repository is an unrefactored MATLAB snapshot and does not include the converted model files.

Memory labels depend on the paper's twofold up-regulation and half down-regulation cutoffs.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.78
data existence: 0.85
data adequacy: 0.8
analysis feasibility: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.9
